Definition: from G4253 and G5225; to exist before, i.e. (adverbially) to be or do something previously:--+ be before(-time).
BiblicalUsage: Prouparcho means to exist before, to be or do something previously. Simon the sorcerer had beforetime in the city used sorcery and bewitched the people of Samaria, and Pilate and Herod were made friends together that same day, for before they were at enmity between themselves.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that before is the word of change: Simon was a sorcerer before, and Pilate and Herod were enemies before, and the gospel makes befores into afters.
